newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-CAMPBELL AND STRANG REVIVE ZIMBABWE AGAINST INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CAMPBELL AND STRANG REVIVE ZIMBABWE AGAINST INDIA.

text.p: A 94-run partnership between captain Alistair Campbell and Paul Strang enabled Zimbabwe to recover to 236 for eight in their one-day international against India in a triangular series match on Monday.

The pair came together with Zimbabwe at a hesitant 51 for three in the 15th over after the Flower brothers, Grant and Andrew, had been dismissed in quick succession following the early loss of opener Andy Waller.
Campbell and Strang began cautiously against some tidy Indian bowling before accelerating.
Leg-spinning all-rounder Paul Strang dominated the early part of the partnership making 31 of the first 50 but Campbell soon caught up.
Both finally perished on the long-on boundary, Strang for 47 in 87 balls and Campbell for 61 from only 70 deliveries, to leave Zimbabwe on 172 for five in the 41st over.
They were boosted to their eventual total by a spectacular 40 in 32 balls from Craig Evans.
